Tout commence en 2009, à Perpignan. Fréd: It all started in 2009, in Perpignan. Frédéric Molas and Sébastien Rassiat, two young audiovisual students, adapted an American concept then emerging on YouTube: the angry review. The principle — pick a bad video game or a childhood cartoon and review it with humour, rage and exaggeration — filmed in Frédéric's teenage bedroom with a simple camcorder.
Quinze ans plus tard, la chaîne principa: Fifteen years later, the main channel has over 3.8 million subscribers. A second channel, Le Bazar du Grenier, has nearly 2 million. Together they total more than 2 billion views. Production has gone professional — each video can cost up to €10,000 — but the concept remains intact: revisiting retro games and forgotten cartoons, with over-the-top humour and deliberately cartoonish fits of rage.
Frédéric incarne le \"vieux con\" râleur: Frédéric plays the grumpy "old git", Sébastien a calmer role. This duo built on contrast, and absolute loyalty to a retro, nostalgic signature, remains the engine of a channel that has accompanied a whole Club Dorothée generation.
Une chaîne qui a réussi l'exploit de res: A channel that has managed the feat of staying true to its concept while evolving — rare at this scale on YouTube. The humour is still relevant, the nostalgia works wonderfully, and the duo has professionalised its production without losing the authenticity of the early episodes. After 15 years, it's still a pleasure to watch Frédéric get worked up and Sébastien calm him down.
Derrière le côté \"mauvais jeux et crise: Behind the "bad games and tantrums" side, there's real work on staging, editing and cultural creation. The channel recalls the codes, references and games that marked a whole generation — and that's precisely why it has such extraordinary longevity. A small drawback: those unfamiliar with retro culture or the '90s may miss many references.
